 Prankster pretends to steal $10 from Michigan pizza worker. His response struck a chord online 
 "Listen dude, I'm not in the mood for this crap right now," the pizza worker said. "You think this is funny, don't you?" 
 By Matt Stefanski • 
 Published October 30, 2026 • 
 Updated on October 30, 2026 at 7:34 pm 
 BOOKMARKER 
 NBC10 Boston/NECN 
 FILE
 An online fundraiser has raised nearly $600,000 for a Michigan grocery store worker whose emotional reaction to an apparent prank while on the job went viral, resonating with people around the world.
 Original footage of the encounter shows the worker, identified through a GoFundMe fundraiser as Walt Z., a Red Baron employee who was stocking pizzas inside a Meijer store. Video of the incident, which has been widely shared on social media, captured the moment a prankster approached and pretended to steal $10 from Walt via his cellphone, eliciting a strong reaction.

 The prankster appeared to play a sound that mimics an Apple Pay transaction and told Walt he took $10 from him.
 "Listen dude, I'm not in the mood for this crap right now," Walt said. "You think this is funny, don't you?"
 Walt said he was going to report the prankster shortly before footage showed him talking to what appeared to be store employees. Visibly shaken, the Red Baron employee confronted the prankster and swore at him, with the prankster insisting "it's just a joke."
 "I don't know if you're recording me or not, I don't know what's going on, but I don't need this crap right now," Walt said.
 "It's not that deep, man...It's just a joke, bro, it's just a joke," the prankster responded.

 But to Walt, it wasn't. 
 "My life is hard enough as it is. I don't need this crap. I got kids at home that went to bed without me right now, and I was supposed to be home an hour ago, and I'm still out here working," he explained. "And I got to get up at five in the morning and do 10 more stores, so this is not a joke to me."
 The prankster repeatedly apologized, but Walt questioned his sincerity, saying he thought the man was smirking.
 "You're probably making money off of this, and I can't even pay my godda-- mortgage, and I got four kids at home," the worker said. 
 The internet has overwhelmingly thrown its support behind Walt, with people saying his emotions and struggles are relatable.
 "I'm with WALT," one commenter wrote.
 "God bless the working man," another added.
 Red Baron Pizza posted about Walt on social media following the encounter, writing, "He's still here. He's got a fan club. Including us."
 "Employee of the month nominations are closed," the post added. "You know why."
